title: ClockTimer state and transition specification
definition: Coordinated state regions: trip lifecycle, focus/workflow, ClockTimer phase, goals/ranges, recognition and pending operations. Combine region attributes; do not enumerate their Cartesian product.
priority: System interruption first; a valid fully formed continuation owns its prefix before shorter conflicting commands. Within a tier, no new total command ranking is proposed.

symbols.skippable: Intermediate feedback is suppressed when this utterance continues; UI action still executes immediately.

sources: app.js: endCurrentIntervalOrTrip, parseVoiceEntryTranscript, installSpeechCommand, WMOFSpeechAvailability, interface transaction adapter
ClockTimer.js: lifecycle, available_actions, active intervals, restoreState
TripAggregates.js: shared counted/percent/banked rules; TripLog.js: aggregation
test_invariants: UI focus, trip phase and enabled commands agree after every transition.
Immediate optimistic outcome; no server write before validation accepts.
Rejected action restores exact checkpoint and cancels dependent actions.
A new editor never reuses a prior value or confirmation flag.
Delayed close events cannot clear or close a newer editor.
Sync Off preserves microphone visibility and recognition.
One utterance cannot execute both a short command and its preempting continuation.
Returning from Trip Log preserves underlying editor value and surface.
Ready / End Trip uses one immutable timestamp for end/start boundary.
End <break type> OK skips question and dialog; standalone final End <break type> shows both.
Scheduled Start accepts a valid duration with or without the Standard Time prefix.
Break Selector is pointer-only; voice start commands use a typed OK/Cancel dialog.
Localized command patterns dispatch neutral interval identifiers; core logic does not parse English break names.
Only the End command matching the active semantic interval type is eligible.
Recognition off/sleep while voice editing switches to keypad and preserves value.
Trip summary stays until OK/Cancel; no automatic editor open.
A spoken range command announces Viewing once and suppresses mode feedback.
Every suppressed component identifies its rule and suppressing owner; optional is not the same as skippable.
review_points: Audit all legacy transition guards against implementation; a prose guard is not an executable predicate.
Specify each transition reducer and server payload/schema exactly before treating the chart as a rebuild specification.
Prove remote-write idempotency and valid-command retry behavior without altering shared audit semantics unsafely.
Enumerate all clock subphases, scheduled-start boundaries, simultaneous event ordering and precedence from model code.
Specify settings draft/save/cancel behavior per settings section, including focus return and validation errors.
Attach automated and production-version evidence to every transition; keep unverified paths gray.
Confirm preferred mode grouping and state names.
Approve the proposed presentation priority tiers; eligibility is dynamic, not a single fixed numeric rank.
Review conditional Lunch question and automatic late-break restart branches.
Confirm whether authentication/settings/training should be added beyond mainline scope.
Voice/screen lane boxes stay at their original heights in the reset view; rotation changes the projection only.

contracts.UI: Apply optimistic outcome immediately. Commands that are client-only do not access remote persistence.
contracts.server: For commands requiring persistence, validate before any write. Rejection restores the checkpoint and cancels dependent operations.
contracts.retry: Local transient storage failures retain optimistic UI and retry asynchronously with 150 ms exponential delay capped at 2000 ms. Abort ends retries. Remote-write retry/idempotency contract remains unresolved.
contracts.time: Durations and boundaries are milliseconds; absolute dates are timezone-aware. Finishing and confirming a new trip are separate user actions, not an automatic continuous boundary.
contracts.summary: Trip Summary can be requested at any time and speaks totals for every trip in selected range except current active trip. No data renders/speaks No trip data available. Both paths hold until OK/Cancel. trip-ended/system adds Say OK to start a new trip LAST; requested/voice or pointer suppresses that prompt and returns to prior focus on OK/Cancel. Range refresh preserves invocation.
contracts.voicepad: Voicepad access while disabled requests explicit recognition enable. OK enables recognition before opening; Cancel preserves current surface. Sleep/off while editing automatically preserves value and opens keypad.
contracts.settings: Settings focus coexists with trip/clock/range regions. Closing settings restores prior focus; persistence rejection restores state and dependent changes.
contracts.locale: Semantic state/range IDs remain stable. UI text, spoken command vocabulary, recognition patterns and announcement templates belong to the selected language pack.
contracts.aggregation: TripAggregates shared calculations: latest row wins per String(id); anonymous rows remain distinct. Range bounds inclusive from CalendarRange.tripWindow. Counted time uses persisted counted milliseconds, fallback actual; active trip counted=max(allotted,counted). percent=standard/counted (null at zero); banked=round(standard/goalPercent-counted). Summary includes both production/nonproduction, excludes running/current ID. Log keeps its production filter and existing active-trip inclusion rule. Results are immutable state.tripAggregates children, UI invocation stays state.tripSummary.
contracts.login: Main page authenticates an admin-assigned four-digit login ID and four-digit PIN. Database primary user ID remains distinct. PIN stored as bcrypt hash. Main-page connect-pin validates exact ASCII digits and leading zeros; other pages retain connect username/password. Failed match resets ID entry. Server enforces per-ID and per-origin limits. Admin assignment requires modify-users permission and target access. English Voice selects four-digit login; User or Username (including User name) selects legacy login. Both commands clear all inputs and repeat the destination prompt, including same-mode loopbacks. Tiny pointer buttons switch modes. Recognition state is preserved; speech requires listening.
contracts.login-input: ID prompt Please login using voice; four digits and OK enter PIN stage, announcing Password. Cancel in either stage clears both and repeats ID prompt. PIN cells render *. On success English speech is Login successful, say standard time or ready at. Off/sleep preserves stage and digits; pointer entry remains available. Wake/on resumes the same stage. English vocabulary and messages are selected-language resources. Recognition status and enable/wake control are visible in both login methods. Only listening exposes login voice commands; pointer/keyboard controls remain available unless login is pending. Recognition lifecycle and local digit/method commands bypass the persistence queue. Rejected pending switches return immediately. Recognition events do not replay login prompts; existing recognition feedback owns its announcement.
